# Implement TLS Channel Bindings

## Priority: Medium 🟡
**Security Enhancement for v0.2.0**

## Description

Add support for TLS channel bindings to prevent MITM attacks when Kerberos is used over TLS-protected transports. This binds the Kerberos authentication to the specific TLS session.

## Requirements

### 1. Channel Binding Types

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum ChannelBindingType {
    /// tls-unique (RFC 5929)
    TlsUnique(Vec<u8>),
    /// tls-server-end-point (RFC 5929)
    TlsServerEndPoint(Vec<u8>),
    /// tls-exporter (RFC 9266)
    TlsExporter(Vec<u8>),
}
```

### 2. GSS Channel Bindings Structure

```rust
/// RFC 2744 Section 3.11
#[repr(C)]
pub struct GssChannelBindings {
    initiator_addrtype: u32,
    initiator_address: Vec<u8>,
    acceptor_addrtype: u32,
    acceptor_address: Vec<u8>,
    application_data: Vec<u8>,
}

impl GssChannelBindings {
    pub fn from_tls(binding: ChannelBindingType) -> Self {
        match binding {
            ChannelBindingType::TlsUnique(data) => Self {
                initiator_addrtype: 0, // GSS_C_AF_UNSPEC
                initiator_address: vec![],
                acceptor_addrtype: 0,
                acceptor_address: vec![],
                application_data: data,
            },
            // ...
        }
    }
}
```

### 3. Integration with Context

```rust
impl Context {
    pub fn set_channel_bindings(&mut self, cb: ChannelBindings) -> Result<()> {
        // Validate binding type
        match &cb {
            ChannelBindings::Tls(binding_type) => {
                // Convert to GSS format
                let gss_cb = GssChannelBindings::from_tls(binding_type.clone());

                // Apply to GSS context
                #[cfg(unix)]
                {
                    self.inner.set_channel_bindings(gss_cb)?;
                }
            }
        }

        self.config.channel_bindings = Some(cb);
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

## TLS Integration

### Extract from rustls
```rust
use rustls::Session;

fn extract_channel_binding(session: &Session) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    // For tls-unique
    session.get_negotiated_tls_unique()
        .map(|data| data.to_vec())
}
```

## Testing

### Unit Tests
```rust
#[test]
fn test_channel_binding_creation() {
    let binding = ChannelBindingType::TlsUnique(vec![0x01, 0x02, 0x03]);
    let gss_cb = GssChannelBindings::from_tls(binding);

    assert_eq!(gss_cb.application_data, vec![0x01, 0x02, 0x03]);
    assert_eq!(gss_cb.initiator_addrtype, 0);
}

#[test]
fn test_channel_binding_validation() {
    // Test with mismatched bindings
    let client_cb = ChannelBindingType::TlsUnique(vec![0x01]);
    let server_cb = ChannelBindingType::TlsUnique(vec![0x02]);

    // Should fail authentication
    assert!(verify_bindings(client_cb, server_cb).is_err());
}
```

### Integration Test
```rust
#[test]
#[ignore] // Requires TLS server
fn test_tls_channel_binding_e2e() {
    // Setup TLS connection
    let stream = TlsStream::connect("server.example.com:443")?;

    // Extract binding
    let binding = extract_channel_binding(&stream)?;

    // Create Kerberos context with binding
    let mut ctx = Context::new(config)?;
    ctx.set_channel_bindings(ChannelBindings::Tls(
        ChannelBindingType::TlsUnique(binding)
    ))?;

    // Authenticate - will fail if bindings don't match
    let token = ctx.initial_token()?;
    assert!(!token.is_empty());
}
```

## Platform Considerations

### Linux (OpenSSL)
- Use `SSL_get_finished()` for tls-unique
- Use `SSL_get_peer_certificate()` for tls-server-end-point

### macOS (Security.framework)
- Use `SSLCopyPeerCertificates()` for certificate
- May need to use lower-level APIs for tls-unique

### Windows (SChannel)
- Use `QueryContextAttributes()` with `SECPKG_ATTR_UNIQUE_BINDINGS`

## Documentation

### Update USAGE.md
```markdown
## Channel Bindings

Prevent MITM attacks by binding Kerberos to TLS session:

```rust
// With rustls
let (stream, binding) = establish_tls_with_binding("server.com")?;

let mut ctx = Context::new(config)?;
ctx.set_channel_bindings(ChannelBindings::Tls(
    ChannelBindingType::TlsUnique(binding)
))?;
```

Supported binding types:
- `tls-unique`: Most secure, requires TLS 1.2
- `tls-server-end-point`: Works with all TLS versions
- `tls-exporter`: TLS 1.3+ only
```
